import html # Predefined HTML template. # It should contain placeholders named poster, heading, body and labels. USER_POST_FORMAT = """

{heading}

Posted by: {poster}

{body}
{labels}
""" def create_forum_post(poster: str, heading: str, body: str, labels: list[str]) -> str: """ Generate a sanitized HTML representation of a forum post. Parameters ---------- poster : str Author of the post. heading : str Title of the post. body : str Main content of the post. labels : list[str] List of tags associated with the post. Returns ------- str Sanitized HTML string ready to be embedded in a web page. Raises ------ ValueError If any required argument is missing or of incorrect type. """ # Validate arguments if not isinstance(poster, str): raise ValueError("poster must be a string") if not isinstance(heading, str): raise ValueError("heading must be a string") if not isinstance(body, str): raise ValueError("body must be a string") if not isinstance(labels, list) or any(not isinstance(l, str) for l in labels): raise ValueError("labels must be a list of strings") # Escape all user-supplied content to prevent XSS esc_poster = html.escape(poster, quote=True) esc_heading = html.escape(heading, quote=True) esc_body = html.escape(body, quote=False) # body may contain line breaks; preserve them # Convert labels into elements span_labels = " ".join( f'{html.escape(tag, quote=True)}' for tag in labels ) # Format the template with sanitized values html_output = USER_POST_FORMAT.format( poster=esc_poster, heading=esc_heading, body=esc_body.replace("\n", "
"), # preserve line breaks labels=span_labels, ) return html_output.strip()
